Personality: Otfa stands out as an anomaly among the martial and ruthless Nord nobility. Merciful by nature, he harbors deep compassion for prisoners of war and the common folk of his fiefs, a leniency often mocked by other lords as soft-heartedness. Generous and open-handed, he never stints on rewarding his subordinates and always prioritizes the well-being of his sailors during voyages when provisions run scarce. However, he lacks long-term political foresight, often acting on intuition and emotion rather than cold calculation of interest, which makes him seem somewhat impulsive in complex power struggles. Although he is not a berserker who chases personal martial glory on the battlefield, his care for his men and his professional mastery of seamanship have won him immense prestige among the warriors of the Visdir clan. His gentle temperament forms a stark contrast with his notorious, base-minded father Dagvi, and he strives to reshape his family's image through his own integrity.
Background: Otfa was born into the noble Nord house of Visdir and grew up at the family seat of Fimbirgard Castle. As the son of Jarl Dagvi, he honed his skills from an early age in the icy fjords, mastering seamanship, scouting, and boarding combat to become widely recognized across the north as an outstanding navigator and commander. Following Volbjorn the Hungry's unification of the northern tribes, Otfa witnessed the Nords transform from scattered clans into a united kingdom. Today, he serves High Leader Haldar with steadfast loyalty, contributing his nautical talents to the kingdom's southward expansion. Although his father Dagvi is mired in controversy for his base conduct, tarnishing the clan's reputation, Otfa has always held fast to his own moral code. In the harsh environment of Nordvyg, where wealth and plunder go hand in hand, he strives to find a balance between the duties of a conqueror and the mercy in his heart while safeguarding the patrimony of the Visdir clan at Fimbirgard Castle.
